title: How far does a near-solid suit stretch?
author_notes: EC-055 checkpoint-3 coverage: a bid_sizing scenario with only one trump offered (Spades), so the decision is purely how many tricks this specific holding supports, not which suit to choose. Contrast with bid_training_006-010, which each compare two trump candidates. Ace-King-Queen-Jack of Spades gives four near-certain trump winners once trumps are drawn; the King of Hearts and Queen of Diamonds are conditional side cards, and the nine/seven of Spades are length tricks that depend on the suit running. Independent hand; ratings are authored judgments, not probabilities or guaranteed outcomes.

feedback.title: Safe, but leaves strength on the table
feedback.summary: Four is a secure floor for this holding, but it undersells four near-certain trump honors without claiming anything conditional.
points: Control: Ace-King-Queen-Jack of Spades are four trump honors, a fact you can check directly against the hand shown.
This target does not need the King of Hearts, the Queen of Diamonds, or either low Spade to be worth anything.
A stronger target is defensible from this same hand; four is not wrong, just conservative.

feedback.title: Matches the visible trump control
feedback.summary: Five uses the four trump honors plus one plausible contribution from the King of Hearts or a promoted low Spade, without depending on both.
points: Control: four trump honors (Ace-King-Queen-Jack of Spades) are the foundation for this target.
Probable, not certain: the King of Hearts is a likely but conditional side winner; either low Spade could also be promoted once higher Spades are gone.
This does not require every conditional card to land — one of several plausible sources is enough for the fifth trick.

feedback.title: Needs more than one thing to go right
feedback.summary: Six asks for both the King of Hearts and a promoted low Spade, not just one of them.
points: The four trump honors alone do not reach six; both remaining sources of extra tricks are conditional, not established.
The Queen of Diamonds is unsupported (only a doubleton) and is not a safer alternative source for this target.
This is not an unreasonable attempt, but it depends on more than the visible strength guarantees.

feedback.title: Asks for nearly everything to work
feedback.summary: Seven needs the King of Hearts, the Queen of Diamonds, and both low Spades to all contribute — far more than this hand's controls support.
points: Four trump honors are a strong start, not seven tricks' worth of established winners on their own.
Stacking every conditional card in the hand together is not the same as counting established winners.
A lower target is more defensible. This assessment does not predict the exact deal outcome.
